title: RT-017 canonical current-version snapshot v1
description: Exact, path-free result of a point lookup in one RT-014 per-report catalog. The provider derives the opaque catalog key from report_key, validates catalog.head and catalog.jsonl, verifies the latest object through SharedEvidenceStore.read_version(report_key, canonical_sha256), and returns no object_id, catalog_key, path, body, tenant or credential field.
semanticRules: The JSON object contains exactly the five required properties; missing or additional properties are rejected.

catalog_key is derived locally from the frozen RT-014 formula r_ + lowercase unpadded RFC 4648 base32(SHA-256(domain || UTF-8(report_key))[0:16]); the provider never accepts catalog_key from a caller.
The provider performs exactly one report-key point lookup. It does not enumerate report catalogs or shared objects and exposes no enumeration, path, object-id, rollback or delete API.

catalog.head and every catalog.jsonl line must be strict duplicate-key-free UTF-8 JSON whose raw bytes equal RFC 8785 JCS; their exact frozen RT-014 field sets, scalar types, grammars, revision/count, raw-byte hash and latest-entry relationships are revalidated.

Every opened directory and file is dir-FD anchored, O_NOFOLLOW, exact-case and exact-Unicode named. Files must be single-link regular files and must retain the same device, inode, mode, link count, size, mtime and ctime through the read. Parent reachability is rechecked before return.
The selected canonical_sha256 is passed with the requested report_key to public SharedEvidenceStore.read_version. Any missing or drifting object fails closed.
The catalog is read again after object verification. Any head or JSONL byte change fails closed rather than returning an already-stale current snapshot.
catalog_head_sha256 is lowercase SHA-256 of the exact canonical catalog.head file bytes; catalog_revision equals the validated head_revision and entry_count.
The null/default provider always returns the stable unavailable failure and never inspects environment variables, the current working directory, catalogs or objects.
